3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Petr, Valken and Iosef were seated.
3.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Admin_Monica_Barred"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_Force"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_LesteKicked"] == true)) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Admin_Monica_Barred"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_Force"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_LesteKicked"] == true)) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Lileas_GendermariePromise"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Lileas_GendermariePromise"] == true) == false)

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: The meeting concluded as the sun set over the concrete jungle that was Holsord.

6.speaker: Petr Vectern
6.text: “We knew that keeping the same budget for the military would cause for some concern from you.”

7.speaker: Player
7.text: “It is a pleasure to work with you Iosef and Valken. You are true sons of Sordland who have served and continue to serve well.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “The military is a top priority for our administration and the Sordish people who hold it in high esteem.”

27.speaker: Valken Kruger
27.text: “Once war or conflict comes knocking, that is when you will realize.”

28.speaker: Iosef Lancea
28.text: “The Ministry of Defense is disappointed about the lack of additional funds.”

30.speaker: Iosef Lancea
30.text: “To say that the Ministry of Defense is furious about the reduction of the military budget would be an understatement.”

32.speaker: Petr Vectern
32.text: “Hopefully the allocated money helps our defense needs.”

33.speaker: Iosef Lancea
33.text: “The Ministry of Defense is content with the additional funds.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “I'd be willing to support the military in other ways. We could come to an agreement.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “Resources were more needed elsewhere. The military has always been well funded.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “It is unfortunate that we weren't able to allocate resources. But, the decision is already made.”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “This is a new age where the military is not top priority. We are going to transform to a new Sordland.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “The increase of the military budget is for national security which is threatened by Rumburg and other nations.”

39.speaker: Valken Kruger
39.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces is a symbol of unity and strength.”

41.speaker: Iosef Lancea
41.text: “We will do all that is necessary to protect this soil.”

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: “Should we move on to the spending choice?”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “Sure. I want to hear the suggestions.”

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “The important thing is we put these funds to good use as the people will need proof of our success in the military.”

46.speaker: Iosef Lancea
46.text: “I'm sure that the people will approve something new and bold from us.”

48.speaker: Petr Vectern
48.text: “The increase of the military budget leaves us with big questions about how to utilize it.”

49.speaker: Iosef Lancea
49.text: “There was a lot of debate at the Ministry which resulted in two factions of thought.”

50.speaker: Iosef Lancea
50.text: “The first faction is in favour of enlarging the armed forces by enlisting more men while the second faction is in favour of purchasing better military equipment instead.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “What is the argument for increasing the size?”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “What is the argument for purchasing better equipment?”

53.speaker: Iosef Lancea
53.text: “The armed forces are behind in terms of military equipment in comparison to our neighbours.”

54.speaker: Valken Kruger
54.text: “No matter how many advanced weapons and systems we buy, our enemies can overcome them.”

55.speaker: Valken Kruger
55.text: “Some of our neighbours have larger populations and thus a larger armed force.”

56.speaker: Iosef Lancea
56.text: “Theoretically numbers alone don't determine the strength balance.”

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “Purchase better equipment and begin a modernisation programme.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “Enlarge the Armed Forces with an expansion programme.”

68.speaker: Iosef Lancea
68.text: “Glad we made the right choice on this. I'll make the necessary arrangements.”

69.speaker: Valken Kruger
69.text: “Thank you for the right choice. The expansion will begin right away.”

70.speaker: Iosef Lancea
70.text: “That is unfortunate but as you command, Mr. President.”

71.speaker: Valken Kruger
71.text: “As you wish. But the decision will be negative for our old doctrine.”

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: The generals were waiting for the word.

77.speaker: Petr Vectern
77.text: “Enlisting more soldiers to the armed forces could also minimize the unemployment issue.”

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “I don't think investing in better equipment is the way.”

81.speaker: Player
81.text: “A vast Armed Forces is my preference.”

84.speaker: Valken Kruger
84.text: “Sir, I will be frank. Rumburg fields three times our force.”

85.speaker: Valken Kruger
85.text: “I think we can agree on that.”

87.speaker: Iosef Lancea
87.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces are already large enough.”

88.speaker: Valken Kruger
88.text: “We cannot beat an overwhelmingly large enemy like Rumburg without numbers.”

89.speaker: Iosef Lancea
89.text: “We are heading to an era of modern combat which requires modern tools to adapt.”

90.speaker: Petr Vectern
90.text: “I hope the decision is in the interest of all.”

91.speaker: Petr Vectern
91.text: “I'd like to extend my thanks for your attendance.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “The military is important but it is not a priority right now.”

95.speaker: Iosef Lancea
95.text: “We request any support we can get at this point.”

96.speaker: Iosef Lancea
96.text: “We live in a geostrategic region with potential volatility.”

97.speaker: Iosef Lancea
97.text: “How come a matter of defense has not been prioritised as more important?”

99.speaker: Petr Vectern
99.text: “We know that there have been high hopes but the President has made his decision to prioritise other branches.”

100.speaker: Valken Kruger
100.text: “This is disastrous and will destroy the Armed Forces as we know it.”

101.speaker: Iosef Lancea
101.text: “This is the age of Rumburg expansionism and here we are cutting funding for the military.”

102.speaker: Iosef Lancea
102.text: “We need money and materials, Mr. President , not excuses.”

103.speaker: Iosef Lancea
103.text: “I have been planning to improve the quality of the armed forces by buying better military equipment.”

104.speaker: Petr Vectern
104.text: “How would that be possible without funds?”

106.speaker: Iosef Lancea
106.text: “If we relieve half the forces that could create enough of a surplus then we could invest in new equipment.”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “Relieving half the armed forces sounds risky at best and destructive at worst.”

110.speaker: Valken Kruger
110.text: “We are barely matching the size of half our neighbours while the other half have armies two times bigger than ours.”

111.speaker: Valken Kruger
111.text: “How on earth would discharging half the armed forces and buying new gear solve our defense issues?”

112.speaker: Player
112.text: “A better equipped smaller force is much more preferable.”

114.speaker: Iosef Lancea
114.text: “Quality over quantity is the right strategy for the future of warfare.”

115.speaker: Iosef Lancea
115.text: “We are two decades behind in gear and training due to the size and sluggishness of the forces.”

116.speaker: Petr Vectern
116.text: “The reduction of the army would cause more unemployment which could hurt the administration.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “Leave the military untouched. There is no reason to break a working structure and risk defense weakness.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “Reduce size and buy better equipment with surplus. Let's reform the army and create a smaller better equipped force.”

119.speaker: Iosef Lancea
119.text: “Unfortunate but as you wish, Mr. President.”

120.speaker: Valken Kruger
120.text: “I can hardly say that I welcome this change.”

121.speaker: Iosef Lancea
121.text: “Excellent. I shall begin the plans immediately.”

122.speaker: Valken Kruger
122.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces will stand strong. We'll maintain our structure.”

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: Iosef and Valken looked at each other.

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “The military makes do. I'm sure you talented gentlemen will find ways to circumvent the cuts efficiently.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “We don't need a powerful military in this day and age.”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “There is not much to be done. The sooner you accept the fact the better.”

127.speaker: Iosef Lancea
127.text: “You have broken promises but I did not expect you to betray the military.”

128.speaker: Iosef Lancea
128.text: “Do not expect the Sordish Armed Forces to be a capable force after these budget changes.”

129.speaker: Petr Vectern
129.text: “Gentlemen. Please. Let's calm down. No need to cause a ruckus.”

130.speaker: Valken Kruger
130.text: “Tell that to the hundreds of thousands that will lose their employment and the honorable general staff of the Armed Forces.”

131.speaker: Valken Kruger
131.text: “You don't mean it but it has been done.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “The Armed Forces is not as important as it claims to be. Therefore the right choice has been made.”

133.speaker: Player
133.text: “We mean no insult to the Armed Forces. There are simply no resources left.”

134.speaker: Valken Kruger
134.text: “What will you do when a defense threat emerges? Call the police?”

135.speaker: Iosef Lancea
135.text: “We expected much more from you, Mr. President. You have let us down.”

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: Iosef and Valken were angry, but there was not much that could be done about it.

138.speaker: Iosef Lancea
138.text: “Know that I won't ever forget your great deed.”

139.speaker: Valken Kruger
139.text: “We are surrounded by jackals as our intelligence and General Staff indicates.”

140.speaker: Valken Kruger
140.text: “It means a lot that the administration sees eye to eye with it.”

141.speaker: Valken Kruger
141.text: “I salute you for this right decision.”

142.speaker: Valken Kruger
142.text: “All spending topics will be addressed so the people can be proud of something that is theirs.”

143.speaker: Iosef Lancea
143.text: “Our enemies are both outside and inside the country.”

144.speaker: Iosef Lancea
144.text: “The President has always been supportive of our agenda because he has a strategic mind.”

147.speaker: Valken Kruger
147.text: “Using funds to boost our size would minimize their advantage.”

149.speaker: Valken Kruger
149.text: “It is clear that the only real disadvantage is the one we have in numbers not equipment.”

150.speaker: Valken Kruger
150.text: “A modernisation programme won't mitigate our difference.”

151.speaker: Iosef Lancea
151.text: “I don't think quantity should be our focus.”

152.speaker: Iosef Lancea
152.text: “Reports show that we lack equipment not men for military efficiency.”

153.speaker: Iosef Lancea
153.text: “The era of large assaults and human wave tactics are over.”

154.speaker: Valken Kruger
154.text: “The military circle has been moody after they heard the decision.”

155.speaker: Valken Kruger
155.text: “We are stuck between a rock and a hard place without money. The military suffers from budget overextension in order to keep up with other countries.”

157.speaker: Iosef Lancea
157.text: “Having a large force doesn't necessitate superiority.”

158.speaker: Iosef Lancea
158.text: “This was a betrayal in our eyes.”

159.speaker: Valken Kruger
159.text: “We will need to cut training time, let soldiers go and stop purchasing equipment.”

160.speaker: Iosef Lancea
160.text: “Let's hope that our enemies won't realize our weaknesses.”

169.speaker: Player
169.text: “Where exactly is our army deployed at right now?”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “How do we compare to other armies?”

171.speaker: Valken Kruger
171.text: “This is low compared to 1000 to 1500 hours in other countries like Arcasia, United Contana, Lespia and even Valgsland.”

172.speaker: Iosef Lancea
172.text: “Which branch would you like to know about?”

173.speaker: Valken Kruger
173.text: “The 1st Army is stationed at the Lespia and Wehlen borders to protect the way into the central regions of Sordland.”

175.speaker: Valken Kruger
175.text: “Rumburg fields six active field armies and two reserve armies, together surpassing one million soldiers in the field. Lespia maintains five armies. With ATO deployments included, their numbers rise to nearly 800,000.”

177.speaker: Valken Kruger
177.text: “Our navy is dwarfed by the Valgslandian fleet, which numbers 194 ships. Agnolia fields 81 vessels. They also maintain strong coastal defenses and heavy naval guns guarding their shores.”

178.speaker: Valken Kruger
178.text: “The truth is, we are limited to our near region due to the size and technological level of our naval ships.”

179.speaker: Player
179.text: “How does our Navy compare to others?”

180.speaker: Player
180.text: “How are our capabilities in power projection?”

181.speaker: Iosef Lancea
181.text: “This does cause some issues like friendly fire and missed close air support opportunities.”

182.speaker: Player
182.text: “What is the situation of our army?”

184.speaker: Valken Kruger
184.text: “Our pilots have average experience. They have a total of 450 hours flight time with their craft before they are qualified. This gives them more than enough time to get used to it.”

185.speaker: Valken Kruger
185.text: “Our planes can bomb targets within 400 km radius of their airfield. They have medium range and semi-effective night-time bombing capabilities.”

188.speaker: Player
188.text: “Can you provide the details on our air force?”

191.speaker: Iosef Lancea
191.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_AirForce_Operation"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_AirForce_Pilots"] == true  or 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_AirForce_Support"] == true) == false

201.speaker: Iosef Lancea
201.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Army_ModernQuest"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Army_AreaOperation"] == true  or 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Army_NeighbourSize"] == true) == false

202.speaker: Valken Kruger
202.text: “Our army is quite outdated by today's military standards. Most of our equipment is two decades old.”

203.speaker: Iosef Lancea
203.text: “According to the latest reports from Camp Strongarm, currently, we field six armies totalling up to approximately 400.000 active troops.”

204.speaker: Player
204.text: “Which seas does our Navy currently patrol?”

207.speaker: Iosef Lancea
207.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Navy_Comparison"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Navy_SeaPatrol"] == true  or 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Navy_PowerProjection"] == true) == false

208.speaker: Valken Kruger
208.text: “We are patrolling the Markian Sea, the Grey Strait and the Antacean Sea.”

209.speaker: Valken Kruger
209.text: “The Air Force is trained as an independent tactical support branch which means it assists other branches but doesn't collaborate.”

210.speaker: Player
210.text: “How does our air force work together with other military branches?”

212.speaker: Iosef Lancea
212.text: “To make up for our lack of modern military equipment, we resort to a large number of soldiers which is not really a long term solution.”

213.speaker: Valken Kruger
213.text: “There are ways to improve collaboration with joint operation rooms. Something to think about surely.”

215.speaker: Valken Kruger
215.text: “I have been trying hard to reduce the negative effects of this problem. We don't need a modernisation program. A standardized purchase of lacking equipment would do.”

216.speaker: Iosef Lancea
216.text: “Our navy currently constitutes 59 vessels with a total of 60.000 sailors and support staff.”

217.speaker: Valken Kruger
217.text: “We need more funding towards expanding the military size. Otherwise, our army will be seen as weak.”

219.speaker: Valken Kruger
219.text: “The 3rd Army is near the Agnolian border and the coastal areas facing Valgsland.”

220.speaker: Iosef Lancea
220.text: “Which is a good amount. The real issue we are having is the quality, not quantity.”

222.speaker: Valken Kruger
222.text: “Due to our bitter past our coastal defense force is always on alert. The decimation of our fleet still is not forgotten.”

223.speaker: Valken Kruger
223.text: “Normally the hours per pilot should be higher but due to the lack of funding we can't increase the training times. Fuel costs are rather high.”

224.speaker: Valken Kruger
224.text: “The 2nd Army has a large mountain commando force and it is the most adequately equipped army to face Rumburg.”

226.speaker: Valken Kruger
226.text: “Valgsland fields one active army of around 140,000 troops, a significant portion of them marines. They also maintain three reserve armies that can be mobilized quickly due to their rapid mobilization military structure.”

235.speaker: Valken Kruger
235.text: “At any-time we can field seven air wings composing a total of 130 aircraft that can operate in combat duty. This is enough to subdue most targets.”

237.speaker: Iosef Lancea
237.text: “Any specific one you want to know about?”

239.speaker: Iosef Lancea
239.text: “As you know, these ships are commanded from our main naval base in Conriat where our flagship, SN Renan is docked.”

246.speaker: Iosef Lancea
246.text: “30.000 pilots and support staff work in the Air Force and they are commanded from the Mark Air Force Base in Erlory.”

248.speaker: Iosef Lancea
248.text: “Rumburg’s sheer size stems from its forced conscription laws. In addition, several ducal regions maintain their own forces at their own expense, further bolstering the crown’s strength. They can sustain this scale thanks to their vast gold reserves, much of which flowed in from Rizia over the past decades.”

249.speaker: Iosef Lancea
249.text: “The Lespian army is the most advanced. Arcasian investment and the Alvarez administration’s expansion of the military-industrial complex have accelerated their modernization.”

250.speaker: Player
250.text: “I am not interested in the details.”
250.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_AirForce"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Army"] == true  or Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_SnO_Listened_Navy"] == true) == false

254.speaker: Valken Kruger
254.text: “Lespia’s navy, while smaller at 39 ships, is heavily modernized and highly capable. That figure excludes the ATO fleet of Arcasia, which stations another 35 ships in Falenco and San Mantua.”

255.speaker: Iosef Lancea
255.text: “Our air force currently has 410 planes in the inventory. Out of which only 140 are jet planes that are not in great condition.”

256.speaker: Iosef Lancea
256.text: “Another thing to note is; after the takeover of Heljiland where our navy has led incursion operations to protect Agnolia, we also take part in some joint navy drills as well.”

258.speaker: Iosef Lancea
258.text: “If we had modern support vessels, we could participate in international operations.”

263.speaker: Iosef Lancea
263.text: “If we are to build a truly effective navy, our ships must be equipped with modern radar and sonar systems. Adding outdated vessels to the roster would change little.”

269.speaker: Player
269.text: “I would like to know about the other branches.”

273.speaker: Valken Kruger
273.text: “We often patrol the routes that are close to the shipping lanes. Especially Markian Sea and Grey Strait. The amount of cargo that goes through that area is eye opening.”

274.speaker: Valken Kruger
274.text: “Our navy protects all our coastal regions however, to make sure we are not thinning out our defense, we prioritise certain regions over others. Like Greater Holsord.”

281.speaker: Valken Kruger
281.text: “In terms of our bombing capability, we have an average of 100 meters of precision. This is not great but it is still within the effective radius of the bombs.”

291.speaker: Player
291.text: “Let's hear about the other branches of the armed forces.”

292.speaker: Valken Kruger
292.text: “We have prepared a briefing to convey further details about the current situation of our military.”

293.speaker: Petr Vectern
293.text: “General Valken. Mr. Lancea. Let's start with the briefing.”

300.speaker: Valken Kruger
300.text: “The 2nd Army, our largest force, has been situated by the Rumburg border.”

301.speaker: Iosef Lancea
301.text: “As you can see, the situation is serious. But the solution is not simply to commission more hulls.”

302.speaker: Valken Kruger
302.text: “That's right. We still hold *some* power though. If needed be, we could block the trade at the Markian Sea.”

303.speaker: Iosef Lancea
303.text: “To make up for our weakness, allying ourselves to a naval power could also help protect our seas.”

307.speaker: Player
307.text: “No need to go into details. I have already settled on a decision.”

308.speaker: Iosef Lancea
308.text: “No use complaining now, Valken. Let's look at what we can do with what we have.”

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: Iosef let out a long sigh.

313.speaker: Petr Vectern
313.text: “That will be all for today then.”

344.speaker: Iosef Lancea
344.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Admin_Monica_Barred"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_Force"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_Personal_Festival_LesteKicked"] == true)) == false

373.speaker: Iosef Lancea
373.text: “First off, we have received an updated communication from the Arcasian military command.”

374.speaker: Iosef Lancea
374.text: “Their planes are being moved into Erlory airbase as we speak.”

376.speaker: Player
376.text: “Good. Make sure you keep an eye on them.”

377.speaker: Player
377.text: “Do your best to make them feel at home.”

378.speaker: Player
378.text: “Ensure that they do not forget which country's soil they are on.”

381.speaker: Narrator
381.text: Iosef and Valken looked at each other.

382.speaker: Iosef Lancea
382.text: “First off, we have received an updated communication from the United Contanan military command.”

383.speaker: Iosef Lancea
383.text: “We are keeping them under close surveillance.”

384.speaker: Player
384.text: “Ensure that they do not forget which country's soil they are on.”

386.speaker: Player
386.text: “Good. Make sure you keep an eye on them.”

388.speaker: Player
388.text: “Do your best to make them feel at home.”

389.speaker: Narrator
389.text: Iosef and Valken looked at each other.

390.speaker: Valken Kruger
390.text: “A single wrong move and we will-”

391.speaker: Iosef Lancea
391.text: “Despite my very vocal disagreement with the plan, their warships are approaching the Conriat naval base as we speak.”

392.speaker: Valken Kruger
392.text: “Contanan warships in Conriat. I thought I would never see the day.”

394.speaker: Player
394.text: “Do not cause any trouble. Do you understand?”

396.speaker: Iosef Lancea
396.text: “Now let's move on to our military.”

416.speaker: Iosef Lancea
416.text: “As if the reduction was not enough, you also decided against reinforcing our border.”

418.speaker: Iosef Lancea
418.text: “If I didn't know better, I would say you are intentionally trying to weaken Sordland, Mr. President.”

419.speaker: Player
419.text: “Of course not. How can you even suggest that?”

420.speaker: Player
420.text: “You dare accuse me of treachery, Iosef?”

421.speaker: Player
421.text: “We are sorry but this had to be done.”

422.speaker: Iosef Lancea
422.text: “Cause and effect. That's how I can suggest that.”

425.speaker: Narrator
425.text: We stared down each other. Petr finally interjected.

427.speaker: Narrator
427.text: Iosef's voice was getting louder and louder.

428.speaker: Valken Kruger
428.text: “If Rumburg were to attack we would need to sacrifice many soldiers to hold the line now.”

429.speaker: Valken Kruger
429.text: “This will help our defensive situation to some degree. Units have already built dozens of pillboxes and trenches with tank traps. But it is not enough.”

430.speaker: Iosef Lancea
430.text: “At the very least you decided to fund our new border fortifications against Rumburg.”

522.speaker: Valken Kruger
522.text: “Wehlen commands two armies totaling roughly 300,000 soldiers, though only their professional core is considered highly capable. Agnolia fields three armies amounting to 250,000 troops. They are well equipped, but have not seen combat in over three decades.”

523.speaker: Iosef Lancea
523.text: “Valgsland follows closely. Although they prioritize economic development and social welfare in their budget, CSP funding has allowed them to remain competitive, keeping the gap with Lespia narrow.”

524.speaker: Valken Kruger
524.text: “Rumburg maintains 94 naval vessels. Intelligence suggests nearly a third of those are submarines. They also rely on other GRACE nations to help secure maritime routes and protect their trade networks abroad.”
